units.note: The sentence on the two-fronted formation (ἡ γὰρ τῆς ἀμφιστόμου τάξεως ἰδιότης τοιαύτην ἔχει τὴν χρείαν) is rendered twice in the English (the end of the previous paragraph and 'Such, indeed, is the advantage...'). This is redundancy, not one of the checked error classes, so no finding.

findings.quote: The Roman shields, that is, offered far greater protection, and their swords were far more effective in action, while the Gallic sword could only deliver a downward cut.
findings.problem: The Greek has a lacuna: οἱ μὲν οὖν θυρεοὶ πρὸς ἀσφάλειαν, αἱ δὲ μάχαιραι πρὸς πρᾶξιν μεγάλην διαφορὰν **** ἔχειν, τὴν δὲ Γαλατικὴν καταφορὰν ἔχειν μόνον. The text breaks off after μεγάλην διαφορὰν, and the English reads on as if the sentence were whole, supplying 'far greater' and 'far more effective' (comparatives that are not in the Greek).
findings.proposed_fix: The shields, for protection, and the swords, for effective action, [...] made a great difference [text missing in the Greek], while the Gallic sword has only the downward cut.

units.note: Gap marked ****; the sense is evidently a comparison of Roman and Gallic equipment, but the exact wording is not recoverable.
The asterisk after Μασσαλίας is a footnote or editorial mark, not a gap in the sense.

findings.quote: may exhaust all their own resources before yielding any of what is essential
findings.problem: The Greek is πάσας ἐξελέγχωσι τὰς σφετέρας ἐλπίδας: 'put all their own hopes to the test'. ἐλπίδας is 'hopes', not 'resources'. The English changes the object and the sense.
findings.proposed_fix: may put all their own hopes to the test before yielding any of what is essential
